content: Striae, commonly referred to as stretch marks, are irregular areas of skin that appear as bands, stripes, or lines. These marks typically develop when the skin undergoes rapid stretching, such as during periods of rapid growth, weight gain, or certain medical conditions. Stretch marks are frequently associated with pregnancy, where abdominal enlargement stretches the skin. They can also occur in children who experience rapid weight gain or during the growth spurts of puberty in both males and females. Stretch marks are most commonly found on the breasts, hips, thighs, buttocks, abdomen, and flanks. Initially, they appear as parallel streaks of red, thinned, and glossy skin. Over time, these marks may fade and take on a whitish, scar-like appearance. The affected areas may feel slightly depressed and have a texture that differs from the surrounding normal skin. In some cases, striae may result from abnormal collagen formation or from the use of medications or chemicals that interfere with collagen production. Long-term use of cortisone compounds, as well as conditions such as diabetes, Cushing's disease, and the postpartum period, can also contribute to the development of stretch marks. The causes of striae include a variety of conditions and factors, such as Cushing's syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, pregnancy, puberty, obesity, and the overuse of cortisone-containing skin creams. It is important to seek medical attention if stretch marks appear without an obvious cause, such as pregnancy or rapid weight gain. In such cases, contacting a healthcare provider is recommended to rule out underlying medical conditions. There is no specific treatment for stretch marks. In many cases, the marks may fade or disappear once the underlying cause of skin stretching is resolved. Creams and ointments marketed to prevent stretch marks during pregnancy are generally not effective. When consulting a healthcare provider about striae, they will perform a physical examination and ask detailed questions about the symptoms. These questions may include whether this is the first occurrence of striae, when the marks were first noticed, what medications have been used, whether cortisone skin creams have been applied, and whether there are any other associated symptoms. If the stretch marks are not attributed to normal physical changes, additional diagnostic tests may be conducted to identify any underlying medical conditions.
